items.name: Siem Reap
items.short_description: Gateway to the temples of Angkor, with a lively old-town, circus arts and excellent Khmer dining.
items.image_credit: Photo: Wikipedia/Wikimedia Commons (licence on file page) - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angkor_Wat

items.name: Phnom Penh
items.short_description: Cambodia's riverside capital, where French-colonial boulevards, royal pavilions and street-food markets sit side by side.
items.image_credit: Photo: Wikipedia/Wikimedia Commons (licence on file page) - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phnom_Penh

items.name: Bangkok
items.short_description: A sprawling, energetic capital of golden temples, canals and world-class street food.
items.image_credit: Photo: Wikipedia/Wikimedia Commons (licence on file page) - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangkok

items.name: Kyoto
items.short_description: Japan's former capital: wooden machiya lanes, vermilion torii gates and thousands of temples.
items.image_credit: Photo: Wikipedia/Wikimedia Commons (licence on file page) - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyoto

items.name: Tokyo
items.short_description: A vast metropolis balancing ancient shrines, neon districts and exceptional food.
items.image_credit: Photo: Wikipedia/Wikimedia Commons (licence on file page) - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo

items.name: Hoi An
items.short_description: A lantern-lit UNESCO old town of tailors, riverside cafes and yellow-washed merchant houses.
items.image_credit: Photo: Steffen Schmitz (more photos), CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons - https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3AH%E1%BB%99i_An%2C_Ancient_Town%2C_2020-01_CN-06.jpg

items.name: Singapore
items.short_description: A clean, compact city-state of gardens, hawker centres and striking architecture.
items.image_credit: Photo: Wikipedia/Wikimedia Commons (licence on file page) - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marina_Bay_Sands

items.name: Bali (Ubud)
items.short_description: Bali's cultural heart, set among rice terraces, temples and artisan villages.
items.image_credit: Photo: Vyacheslav Argenberg, CC BY 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons - https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3ABali%2C_Rice_fields%2C_Rice_terraces_in_East_Bali%2C_Indonesia.jpg

items.name: Penang (George Town)
items.short_description: A UNESCO heritage city of street art, clan houses and Malaysia's best hawker food.
items.image_credit: Photo: Wikipedia/Wikimedia Commons (licence on file page) - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Town%2C_Penang

items.name: Phuket
items.short_description: Thailand's biggest island: sweeping beaches, a pastel old town and boat trips into Phang Nga Bay.
items.image_credit: Photo: Wikipedia/Wikimedia Commons (licence on file page) - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phuket_province

items.name: Kampot
items.short_description: A slow riverside town of pepper farms, colonial shophouses and views of Bokor mountain.
items.image_credit: Photo: Wikipedia/Wikimedia Commons (licence on file page) - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampot

items.name: Seoul
items.short_description: A dynamic capital of royal palaces, hillside hanok villages and 24-hour food streets.
items.image_credit: Photo: Wikipedia/Wikimedia Commons (licence on file page) - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul

items.name: Ho Chi Minh City
items.short_description: Vietnam's southern hub of motorbikes, French-colonial landmarks and superb street food.
items.image_credit: Photo: Wikipedia/Wikimedia Commons (licence on file page) - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ho_Chi_Minh_City

items.name: Da Nang
items.short_description: A modern beach city of dragon bridges, marble mountains and the Hai Van mountain pass.
items.image_credit: Photo: Wikipedia/Wikimedia Commons (licence on file page) - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da_Nang

items.name: Hanoi
items.short_description: A thousand-year-old capital of lakes, narrow shophouse streets and pho at dawn.
items.image_credit: Photo: Wikipedia/Wikimedia Commons (licence on file page) - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanoi

items.name: Kuala Lumpur
items.short_description: Malaysia's capital, famed for the Petronas Towers, multicultural food and green pockets.
items.image_credit: Photo: Marcin Konsek, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons - https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3A2016_Kuala_Lumpur%2C_Narodowe_Muzeum_W%C5%82%C3%B3kiennictwa.jpg

items.name: Chiang Mai
items.short_description: A walled northern city of temples, craft markets and mountain scenery.
items.image_credit: Photo: Wikipedia/Wikimedia Commons (licence on file page) - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiang_Mai

items.name: Krabi
items.short_description: Limestone cliffs, hidden lagoons and the beaches of Railay and Ao Nang.
items.image_credit: Photo: Wikipedia/Wikimedia Commons (licence on file page) - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krabi_province

items.name: Koh Rong
items.short_description: A forested island with white-sand beaches, snorkelling and bioluminescent plankton at night.
items.image_credit: Photo: Wikipedia/Wikimedia Commons (licence on file page) - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koh_Rong

items.name: Yogyakarta
items.short_description: Java's cultural capital, a sultan's palace city near Borobudur and Prambanan.
items.image_credit: Photo: Wikipedia/Wikimedia Commons (licence on file page) - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yogyakarta

items.name: Kep
items.short_description: A quiet seaside town famous for its crab market and ferries to Rabbit Island.
items.image_credit: Photo: PsamatheM, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons - https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3AFishing_Boat_off_Kep%2C_Cambodia.jpg

items.name: Battambang
items.short_description: A colonial-era provincial capital known for its arts scene, countryside and the bamboo train.
items.image_credit: Photo: Wikipedia/Wikimedia Commons (licence on file page) - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battambang

items.name: Luang Prabang
items.short_description: A UNESCO-listed riverside town of golden temples, French villas and morning alms.
items.image_credit: Photo: Wikipedia/Wikimedia Commons (licence on file page) - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luang_Prabang

items.name: Sihanoukville
items.short_description: Cambodia's main beach port city and the departure point for the islands.
items.image_credit: Photo: Dmitry Makeev, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons - https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3ASihanoukville._Boat_on_the_sandy_coast.jpg

items.name: Vientiane
items.short_description: The unhurried Lao capital on the Mekong, with golden stupas and riverside night markets.
items.image_credit: Photo: Basile Morin, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons - https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3AWat_Si_Saket_in_its_paved_courtyard_Vientiane_Laos.jpg

items.name: Mondulkiri
items.short_description: Cool highland forest and waterfalls, home to the Bunong people and elephant sanctuaries.
items.image_credit: Photo: Wikipedia/Wikimedia Commons (licence on file page) - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mondulkiri_province

items.name: Ratanakiri
items.short_description: Cambodia's wild north-east: crater lakes, jungle waterfalls and highland villages.
items.image_credit: Photo: Lukas Bergstrom, CC BY 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons - https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3ARatanakiri_waterfall.jpg

items.name: Kratie
items.short_description: A Mekong riverside town best known for sightings of Irrawaddy dolphins.
items.image_credit: Photo: Wikipedia/Wikimedia Commons (licence on file page) - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irrawaddy_dolphin

items.name: Kampong Cham
items.short_description: A calm Mekong river town with a famous bamboo bridge, hilltop temples and rural cycling.
items.image_credit: Photo: Myrmux, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons - https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3AMekongbr%C3%BCcke_bei_Kampong_Cham_4.jpg

items.name: Koh Kong
items.short_description: A mangrove-and-rainforest province on the Gulf of Thailand with waterfalls and kayaking.
items.image_credit: Photo: Christiane Bender, CC BY 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons - https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3A2015_0319_174425_KohKongIsland_Strandidylle.jpg
